Statuses follow the classic BT convention:
  SUCCESS  / FAILURE are terminal for the tick.
  RUNNING  means "not done yet; resume me next tick".

Sequence and Selector implement *memory* semantics: when a child returns
RUNNING, the composite remembers its index and, on the next tick, resumes
directly from that running child (earlier siblings are NOT re-run). The
cursor resets to 0 whenever the composite finishes (SUCCESS or FAILURE).
"""

from enum import Enum


class Status(Enum):
    SUCCESS = "SUCCESS"
    FAILURE = "FAILURE"
    RUNNING = "RUNNING"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Composites / decorators
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Node:
    def tick(self, world) -> Status:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def reset(self):
        """Forget any per-tick memory (running cursor etc.)."""


class Sequence(Node):
    """Succeeds if all children succeed; resumes from the running child."""

    def __init__(self, name, children):
        self.name = name
        self.children = list(children)
        self._index = 0

    def tick(self, world) -> Status:
        while self._index < len(self.children):
            status = self.children[self._index].tick(world)
            if status is Status.RUNNING:
                return Status.RUNNING          # resume here next tick
            if status is Status.FAILURE:
                self._index = 0                # sequence failed: restart later
                return Status.FAILURE
            self._index += 1                   # child succeeded, advance
        self._index = 0                        # all succeeded: restart later
        return Status.SUCCESS

    def reset(self):
        self._index = 0
        for child in self.children:
            child.reset()


class Selector(Node):
    """Tries children left-to-right; resumes from the running child."""

    def __init__(self, name, children):
        self.name = name
        self.children = list(children)
        self._index = 0

    def tick(self, world) -> Status:
        while self._index < len(self.children):
            status = self.children[self._index].tick(world)
            if status is Status.RUNNING:
                return Status.RUNNING
            if status is Status.SUCCESS:
                self._index = 0                # selector succeeded: restart later
                return Status.SUCCESS
            self._index += 1                   # child failed, try next
        self._index = 0                        # all failed: restart later
        return Status.FAILURE

    def reset(self):
        self._index = 0
        for child in self.children:
            child.reset()


class Inverter(Node):
    """Flips SUCCESS <-> FAILURE; passes RUNNING through unchanged."""

    def __init__(self, name, child):
        self.name = name
        self.child = child

    def tick(self, world) -> Status:
        status = self.child.tick(world)
        if status is Status.SUCCESS:
            return Status.FAILURE
        if status is Status.FAILURE:
            return Status.SUCCESS
        return Status.RUNNING

    def reset(self):
        self.child.reset()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Leaves
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Condition(Node):
    """Leaf that only observes the world; never RUNNING."""

    def __init__(self, name, predicate):
        self.name = name
        self.predicate = predicate

    def tick(self, world) -> Status:
        return Status.SUCCESS if self.predicate(world) else Status.FAILURE


class Action(Node):
    """Leaf that mutates the world and may return RUNNING.

    fn(world) -> Status. Named actions append to world.log so tests can
    assert an exact per-tick action trace.
    """

    def __init__(self, name, fn):
        self.name = name
        self.fn = fn

    def tick(self, world) -> Status:
        status = self.fn(world)
        if getattr(world, "log", None) is not None:
            world.log.append((world.tick_no, self.name, status))
        return status


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Guard NPC domain
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

POST = 0  # guard's post position on a 1-D line


class World:
    """Scripted world: 1-D positions; intruder_pos None when absent."""

    def __init__(self, guard_pos=2, intruder_pos=None):
        self.guard_pos = guard_pos
        self.intruder_pos = intruder_pos
        self.tick_no = 0
        self.log = []


def build_guard_tree():
    chase = Action("chase", _chase)
    walk_back = Action("walk_to_post", _walk_to_post)
    idle_scan = Action("idle_scan", _idle_scan)

    return Selector("guard_brain", [
        # intruder visible -> chase it
        Sequence("engage_intruder", [
            Condition("intruder_visible", lambda w: w.intruder_pos is not None),
            chase,
        ]),
        # at post -> idle scan
        Sequence("hold_post", [
            Condition("at_post", lambda w: w.guard_pos == POST),
            idle_scan,
        ]),
        # otherwise -> walk back to post
        walk_back,
    ])


def _chase(world) -> Status:
    if world.intruder_pos is None:              # lost them mid-chase
        return Status.FAILURE
    delta = world.intruder_pos - world.guard_pos
    if delta == 0:                              # apprehended!
        return Status.SUCCESS
    world.guard_pos += 1 if delta > 0 else -1   # one step per tick
    return Status.RUNNING


def _walk_to_post(world) -> Status:
    if world.guard_pos == POST:
        return Status.SUCCESS
    world.guard_pos += 1 if world.guard_pos < POST else -1
    return Status.RUNNING


def _idle_scan(world) -> Status:
    return Status.SUCCESS


def run_ticks(tree, world, n):
    """Advance the world n ticks, ticking the tree once per tick."""
    root_statuses = []
    for _ in range(n):
        world.tick_no += 1
        root_statuses.append(tree.tick(world))
    return root_statuses

def test_sequence_resumes_running_child_without_rerunning_earlier_siblings():
    cond_calls = []

        cond_calls.append(1)
        return Status.SUCCESS

    ran_from = []

    def running_action(world):
        ran_from.append(world.marker)
        return Status.RUNNING

    seq = Sequence("s", [

        Action("long_task", running_action),
        Action("never_reached", lambda w: Status.FAILURE),

    seq.tick({})          # cond + long_task -> RUNNING
